podcast.title: Death Details - February 2, 2004
podcast.body: Wayne Kramer died on February 2nd, 2004, from pancreatic cancer. "He died on February 2nd, 2004 of Pancreatic Cancer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Younger Bands - The Clash
podcast.body: His influence was recognized by younger bands, with The Clash specifically mentioning him in their song "Jail Guitar Doors." "The clash, named check him in a song called Jail Guitar Doors."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-MC5 Criminality and Imprisonment
podcast.body: After the MC5 disbanded in 1972, Kramer became involved in petty crime. A drug conviction in 1975 led to a four-year prison sentence. "The MC5 was done by 1972, and Kramer became a petty criminal. A drug conviction in 1975 sent him to prison for four years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Prison Career
podcast.body: Following his release from prison, Wayne Kramer returned to playing guitar while also working as a carpenter and woodworker. "When he got out, he went back to playing guitar in between working as a carpenter and woodworker."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Prisoner's Charity Work
podcast.body: Wayne Kramer dedicated time to working with a prisoner's charity, collaborating with notable musicians such as Tom Morello, Billy Bragg, Perry Farrell, and Jerry Cantrell of Alice in Chains. "He also worked with a prisoner's charity alongside Tom Morello, Billy Bragg, Perry Farrell, and Jerry Cantrell of Ellison Chains."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Producer and Film Composer
podcast.body: Kramer produced records for other artists and composed music for film. He notably contributed to several film projects for Will Ferrell, including the comedy "Talladega Nights, the ballad of Ricky Bobby," due to Ferrell being a fan. "He also produced records for other people and provided music for film. You know the Will Farrell comedy Talladega Knights, the ballad of Ricky Bobby? Wayne Kramer. In fact, Farrell was such a fan that he used Wayne for a number of his film projects."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
